title: When desire keeps calling itself wisdom
issueStatement: The appetite always has a reason ready: security, beauty, relief, prudence, reward. But after each new reason is obeyed, the heart is still unsettled.
centralInsight: Gurbani exposes greed by asking what actually remains. False wealth fattens anxiety; true wealth travels with the soul and teaches the hand to open.
practicalReflection: Greed is not only having too much. It is the inability to believe that enough can exist while the Giver is still near.
actionPrompt: Before the next grasping move, ask what you are afraid will happen if you stop taking more than this moment actually needs.
searchTerms: training desire to live inside enough

source.shortMeaning: how can the Naam, the Name of the Lord, find its dwelling in the heart; falsehood is a filthy street-sweeper. Cheating is eating a rotting carcass
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: The shabad is blunt on purpose: greed is not styled as ambition or refinement. It is named as corruption that fills life with appetite while leaving no room for Naam to dwell.

source.shortMeaning: Take the Merchandise of the Lord's Praises with you. Your Husband Lord shall see this and approve; those who do not have the Assets of Truth-how can they find peace
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: Here greed is corrected by a better economy. The question is not how much you can gather, but what can actually accompany you and make the soul rich.

source.shortMeaning: One who chants the Praises of the Lord is the greatest of the great; the Lord is close to His humble servant, and His humble servant is close
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: The line contrasts begging for riches with praising the Lord and being kept close in humility. Greed shrinks when nearness becomes more desirable than accumulation.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: Greed in ordinary decisions
daily.issueStatement: Greed rarely arrives announcing itself. It shows up in quick choices, small upgrades, and the quiet assumption that more will steady you.
daily.centralInsight: The Guru makes daily desire visible by asking what your decisions are training you to worship.
daily.practicalReflection: Ordinary wanting shapes the soul long before crisis does. Daily choices reveal whether contentment is being practiced or deferred.
daily.actionPrompt: Before the next purchase, scroll, or grasping impulse, ask whether it will actually nourish you or only extend the craving.

source.shortMeaning: falsehood is a filthy street-sweeper. Cheating is eating a rotting carcass; the pleasures of gold and silver, the pleasures of women, the pleasure
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line meet the part of the day already in front of you.

excerpts.explanation: The ordinary day is where greed usually hides best, so the shabad names it without softness. Daily appetite is exposed through speech, habit, and the small dishonesties that make craving look respectable.

source.shortMeaning: One who calls himself a guru or a spiritual teacher, while he goes around
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line meet the part of the day already in front of you.

excerpts.explanation: The cure is practical, not theatrical. Honest work and open-handed giving retrain desire by reminding the heart that life is for right earning and sharing, not private accumulation.

source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line meet the part of the day already in front of you.

excerpts.explanation: This line slows the appetite down. Greed loses force when the soul begins recognizing Naam as wealth and patience as honor rather than treating delay as deprivation.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: Greed when fear starts talking
pressure.issueStatement: Under pressure, accumulation can feel like wisdom. Fear tells you that keeping more, taking more, or hoarding more is just prudence.
pressure.centralInsight: Gurbani separates provision from panic. Pressure does not justify letting fear rename greed as responsibility.
pressure.practicalReflection: The anxious mind wants visible surplus. The Guru keeps returning the question to trust, truthful work, and what can actually accompany you.
pressure.actionPrompt: When fear says take extra, pause long enough to ask whether you are being guided by care or by scarcity posing as care.

source.shortMeaning: Take the Merchandise of the Lord's Praises with you. Your Husband Lord shall see this and approve; buy that object which will go along with you
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line decide the next tone before urgency does.

excerpts.explanation: Pressure keeps inventing urgent purchases for the soul. Gurbani answers by asking what kind of gain still matters after fear has spent itself and the moment has passed.

source.shortMeaning: This is your chance to meet the Lord of the Universe; vibrate and meditate on the Jewel of the Naam
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line decide the next tone before urgency does.

excerpts.explanation: Scarcity narrows the horizon to the next immediate need. This shabad widens it again by reminding you what human life is for, so fear does not get to define wisdom on its own.

source.shortMeaning: Those who are blessed with Your Mercy obtain the Jewel of the Naam, the Name of the Lord; whatever pleases You comes to pass. As You give, so do we receive
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the line decide the next tone before urgency does.

excerpts.explanation: The line breaks the trance of panic by returning the heart to Hukam. Trust does not erase provision; it stops fear from calling greed responsible.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: Returning after grasping too hard
repair.issueStatement: You already let greed set the terms, and now the mind wants to defend the choice rather than confess the hunger beneath it.
repair.centralInsight: Repair begins when greed is named without euphemism. The Guru turns you back toward truthful earning, honest release, and inner poverty before God.
repair.practicalReflection: What was taken or clung to matters, but so does the desire beneath it. Return is not complete until the heart relearns sufficiency.
repair.actionPrompt: Admit where grasping overruled truth, undo one part of the harm if you can, and practice one concrete act of release today.

source.shortMeaning: how can the Naam, the Name of the Lord, find its dwelling in the heart; falsehood is a filthy street-sweeper. Cheating is eating a rotting carcass
source.lifeApplication: Ask what you are taking in that still leaves the heart poor. Let the next return stay smaller and truer than the slip.

excerpts.explanation: Repair starts with clean naming. The shabad refuses euphemism, which is exactly what the heart needs after greed has already tried to baptize itself as necessity.

excerpts.explanation: Release becomes possible when the soul remembers it was never the final owner. What was grasped can be returned because it was first received under Hukam.

excerpts.explanation: Greed leaves residue in conduct, not only in the original act. This line keeps repair practical by tying inward cleansing to the way you now speak, carry yourself, and move forward.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Training desire to live inside enough
practice.issueStatement: Greed does not usually break through one dramatic renunciation. It weakens when the appetite is retrained in small, repeated acts of enoughness.
practice.centralInsight: Contentment in Gurbani is not passivity. It is disciplined agreement with the Giver, repeated until craving stops sounding like your truest voice.
practice.practicalReflection: Enough has to be practiced because the world catechizes shortage all day long. Desire learns from repetition too.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one appetite that usually asks for more and practice stopping while gratitude is still possible.
